titleText.en: Listen, they request that you stop submitting a listing for your house labeled 'WHERE YOU BROKE MY HEART'.
titleText.noteEn: The Spanish archive leaves its title text empty. The official English text extends the joke by treating the man's heartbreak as a Google Maps house-listing label.

regions.labelEs: LO SIENTO, EL EQUIPO DE GOOGLE MAPS ME HA CONTRATADO.

excludedUnits.rationale: Google Maps is the retained English brand name of the mapping service, not Spanish vocabulary.

applications.explanationEn: Lo and siento form the fixed apology used by one speaker.
Ha is the present helper used for the singular team, and contratado is contratar's unchanged completed-action form.

regions.labelEs: ¡PERO YO NO PUEDO MUDARME A CALIFORNIA!

applications.explanationEn: Puedo changes for the speaker, while mudarme keeps mudar in its dictionary form with me attached.
Me is attached to the end of mudar and identifies the speaker as the person changing homes.

regions.labelEs: ENTONCES SUPONGO QUE ES EL FIN.

applications.explanationEn: Puede carries the possibility meaning, and ser remains in its unchanged dictionary form.
No puede ser is used here as a shocked reaction to a conclusion that the speaker cannot accept.
Escucha is the positive command used with one familiar listener.

regions.labelEs: CUANDO MIRO EN LO PROFUNDO DE TUS OJOS, VEO UN FUTURO PARA NOSOTROS.

applications.explanationEn: Lo turns profundo into a general inner part without naming a masculine noun, so profundo stays masculine singular.
Mira is the positive command used with one familiar listener.
Mira supplies the action, más increases the degree, and profundo stays in its masculine singular form while describing how the looking is done.

regions.labelEs: "LO SENTIMOS, PERO NO TENEMOS IMÁGENES PARA ESTE NIVEL DE ZOOM."

applications.explanationEn: Lo and the plural form sentimos make the conventional apology used by an organization.
Lo fills the same fixed apology slot as in lo siento; the plural sentimos changes the speakers, not lo's role.

cards.answerEn: it (in the fixed apology lo siento, I'm sorry)

cards.noteEn: Use this fixed expression for an apology or when reacting sympathetically to bad news. Learn it as a complete expression instead of translating lo and siento separately.
cards.questionEn: What is the standard way to say “I'm sorry” when apologizing or expressing sympathy?

example.en: I'm sorry. It was a mistake.

cards.answerEn: I feel (in lo siento: I'm sorry)

cards.noteEn: Equipo can also mean equipment; here it names a group of people working together.

example.en: The team is looking for a solution.

cards.answerEn: Use he, has, ha, hemos, habéis, or han followed by the verb’s completed-action form.
cards.noteEn: These are forms of haber, the helper verb used here like English “have.” For most verbs, the completed-action form ends in -ado after an -ar verb and -ido after an -er or -ir verb. This form is called the past participle, and it does not change after haber. How often this tense is used instead of the simple past varies by region.
cards.questionEn: How do you say “have done,” as in “I have finished”?

cards.noteEn: Contratado is the completed-action form of contratar, “to hire.” After a form of haber such as ha, it stays unchanged.

example.es: La empresa ha contratado a Julia.

cards.promptEs: poder + verbo en forma de diccionario
cards.questionEn: How do you say that someone can, could, or may do something?
cards.answerEn: Use a form of poder for the person and situation, then keep the action verb in its unchanged dictionary form.
cards.noteEn: Poder changes to forms such as puedo, puedes, puede, podemos, and pueden for present ability or possibility. Podría can present a possible or imagined option. The following action keeps its -ar, -er, or -ir ending.
Mudarme joins mudar with me. The attached me identifies the speaker as the person changing homes.

cards.promptEs: verbo en forma de diccionario + pronombre unido
cards.questionEn: Where can a short object word such as me, te, lo, or la go with an unchanged action verb?
cards.answerEn: Attach it to the end of the verb and write the result as one word.
cards.noteEn: An unchanged dictionary-form verb ends in -ar, -er, or -ir. Short object words can attach directly: conocer + te becomes conocerte, and ayudar + me becomes ayudarme.
Que introduces a clause after verbs such as creer, saber, esperar, or decir. English often uses “that,” but may leave it unstated.

example.en: I think that Ana is coming.

cards.questionEn: How do you react when something seems impossible or unbelievable?
cards.answerEn: Say no puede ser for “that can't be” or “no way.”
cards.noteEn: No negates the claim, puede is the form of poder used for one situation, and ser stays in its unchanged dictionary form. The expression can reject a fact literally or serve as a surprised reaction.
Escucha is the positive command of escuchar for one friend, peer, or other familiar listener.

cards.promptEs: orden afirmativa para tú: habla, come, escribe
cards.questionEn: How do you give one friend or familiar person a positive command?
cards.answerEn: Use the informal singular command form, often the same form used for “he” or “she” in the present.
cards.noteEn: For many regular verbs, -ar becomes -a and -er or -ir becomes -e: hablar becomes habla, comer becomes come, and escribir becomes escribe. Some common verbs are irregular or change their stem. Negative commands use a different form and are a separate pattern.

cards.answerEn: the (neutral article before an adjective, as in lo mejor)
cards.noteEn: Neutral lo turns an adjective into an abstract idea: lo importante means “the important thing,” not a masculine noun.

example.en: The important thing is to begin.

cards.questionEn: How do you refer to “what is important,” “the difficult part,” or another general quality without naming a noun?
cards.answerEn: Put the unchanged word lo before a masculine-singular adjective: lo importante, lo difícil, lo bueno.
cards.noteEn: Here lo does not stand for a masculine object. It turns the quality into a general idea or aspect, such as lo importante, “what is important.” The adjective stays in its masculine singular form because there is no named noun for it to match.
Lo can turn profundo, “deep,” into the general idea of a deep or innermost part.

example.es: La luz no llega a lo profundo de la cueva.
example.en: The light does not reach the depths of the cave.

cards.promptEs: verbo + adjetivo usado para describir el modo
cards.questionEn: How can words such as claro, alto, or profundo describe how an action is done without adding -mente?
cards.answerEn: In certain common combinations, put the describing word after the verb and keep it in its masculine singular form.
cards.noteEn: A word that normally describes a noun can sometimes work like an English -ly word and describe the action instead: hablar claro, volar alto, respirar profundo. It does not change for the person doing the action. This use is conventional, so it cannot be applied freely to every adjective.

cards.answerEn: deep; deeply (describing how an action is done)
cards.noteEn: Some Spanish describing words can also tell how an action is done. In this use profundo stays in its masculine singular form rather than changing to profundamente.

cards.promptEs: Google Maps: imágenes y nivel de zoom
cards.questionEn: Why does a Google Maps zoom message turn the romantic scene into a joke?
cards.answerEn: Map services may lack imagery at very close zoom levels; the scene treats looking deeply into a person's eyes as if it were zooming into a map.
cards.noteEn: The woman has just joined the Google Maps team. The mapping-service limitation therefore appears where a romantic revelation should be, combining her new job with the literal idea of looking deeper.

example.es: Amplía el mapa para ver la calle.
example.en: Zoom in on the map to see the street.

cards.questionEn: How does a group or organization say “we're sorry” in Spanish?
cards.noteEn: This is the plural counterpart of lo siento. Lo stays fixed, while siento changes to sentimos because the speakers are saying “we feel.” Learn the two words together as an apology rather than translating them literally.
Sentimos normally means “we feel.” In the fixed expression lo sentimos, it is the plural apology used by a group or organization.

cards.answerEn: for; at (a level or setting something is available for)
cards.noteEn: Para can introduce the level or setting that a resource supports. English may use “for” or, with a level, “at.”

example.es: No hay datos para ese nivel de detalle.
example.en: There is no data at that level of detail.

cards.answerEn: no separate English word; links an item to its type
cards.noteEn: Spanish often uses de between an item and the noun that identifies its type. English often puts the type noun first instead: libro de historia becomes “history book.”
Spanish uses the borrowed noun zoom for changing how close or enlarged an image appears.
Spoken on its own with a pause, ya can show that the speaker has just understood what is happening. This differs from its time meaning ‘already.’

example.en: I see... now I understand it.
